sun.upright:
An Aries Sun wants to be first through the door and sort out the mess afterwards, so a card about finishing things sits a bit sideways on you. Death is Scorpio's card, and Scorpio stands five signs from Aries, the angle astrologers call a quincunx. Signs that far apart have almost nothing in common, so they get along by constant small adjustments. The elements make it harder. Your sign runs hot, this card runs deep and wet, and where fire meets water you either get steam or one of them goes out. The one real link is Mars. It rules Aries, and in the traditional system it rules Scorpio as well, so the same engine is driving both of you, pointed in opposite directions.

What that feels like is a strong forward push with nowhere new to put it until something old is closed off. You want the next start, and the card keeps turning you back to a start you made a while ago that has quietly run its course. Winding a thing down is slow and fiddly and nobody claps, which makes it exactly the work you find hardest. I'd guess you already know which thing I mean. The Emperor is Aries's own card, a man on a stone throne who intends to stay there. Have a look at who's lying under the horse in this one. It's a king, and his crown has come off.

At work it's probably the project you fought to get going and now suspect is finished, and relaunching it louder won't bring it back. In the body it's a training habit or a pace you set years ago that's wearing you down, and you'll push through the ache long after it's taught you anything. Pick one thing you began that you already know is over, and be the first to say so out loud.
sun.reversed:
When Death comes up reversed for an Aries Sun, the fire keeps restarting the exact thing that ought to end. You relaunch the finished project under a new name, pick the old argument back up, sign on for one more season, because stopping feels like losing and losing is the one thing your sign can't sit still with. The Mars drive that could make a clean break gets spent defending something that's already gone.

You'll see it in a job you keep threatening to leave and never do, or a rivalry you stir up again whenever it goes quiet. From the outside it looks like commitment. Underneath, it's mostly fear of the empty stretch after a thing ends, when there's nothing left to push against. Let yourself lose one round on purpose. Walk away from an argument you'd normally win, and notice you're still standing.

moon.upright:
An Aries Moon settles by doing something about a feeling straight away. A walk, a row, a decision, anything that turns the churn into movement, and by the evening it's usually passed. Death asks for the one thing your gut refuses, which is to sit inside a loss and let it finish on its own slow clock. This is Scorpio's card, fixed water, and fixed water doesn't hurry for anyone. Fire and water are opposed elements, so there's real friction here, your quick heat against the card's slow depth, with no shared rhythm to fall back on.

Mars rules Aries, and a Mars Moon keeps the body on alert, ready to fix or to fight. When something ends, a friendship, a routine, a place you used to feel at home, your reflex is to book the trip or pick the argument or throw yourself at the gym, anything with a lever to pull. Grief doesn't have a lever, and that helplessness is what really gets under your skin. I've seen plenty of Aries Moons go straight to anger when sadness was the truer feeling, because anger at least goes somewhere. What the card wants is for you to stay with one feeling long enough for it to finish.

Sleep is one place it shows. You lie there wide awake, the body braced for a fight that ended days ago. A friendship is another, someone you've drifted from, where your instinct is to paper over the gap with plans. Some evening soon, sit with one feeling and do nothing about it at all.
moon.reversed:
An Aries Moon with Death upside down treats grief as something to outrun. You stay furious because anger has somewhere to go and sorrow just sits there, and the slow work of feeling a loss through gets slammed shut before it starts. The feeling doesn't leave. It goes underground and comes back as a short fuse, a cupboard door banged, a snapped reply to someone who didn't earn it.

It tends to show in sleep, with the body still braced long after whatever happened, and in a habit you can't drop because stopping would leave you alone with what you won't feel. A partner or a housemate often takes the brunt of it. More activity won't clear it. Name the actual loss under the temper, even just to yourself in the car, and let yourself be sad about it for ten minutes.

rising.upright:
Aries rising arrives fast. Mars rules your chart, and strangers usually meet someone already moving, direct, a bit of a challenge, the first to speak. Death comes in the opposite way. Look at the horse in the picture. It's walking, and nobody in that field can hurry it along or talk it round. Scorpio sits five signs from Aries, the awkward quincunx, so the two never quite agree on tempo, and water meeting your fire throws off steam. The card is pointing at the way you start things, and it suggests an old opening move has run its course.

You might notice your usual way in isn't landing like it did. The charge-straight-in style that used to win you the job, the date, the deal, is getting a cooler reception, and Aries rising tends to read that as a cue to push harder. That's the wrong lever here. Scorpio has a quieter, more watchful way of coming into a room, and the card is offering you some of it. It won't feel natural at first. Mars has a hand in both signs, though, so the force is still yours. It just comes in slower.

With strangers, it's the first impression you've always trusted getting a mixed response. In a new job, it's the eager early push that people read as too much. Walk into your next meeting slower than feels right, say less for the first ten minutes, and see what you pick up when you're not the fastest thing in the room.
rising.reversed:
With Death reversed, Aries rising uses speed as armour. You keep the pace so high that nobody, you included, gets a look at what's finishing underneath. Arrive fast enough, stay busy enough, and you never have to stand still in the gap after something ends. People meet a lot of energy and struggle to find you in it, and when they stop trying, you take that as proof you should push harder.

It shows in first meetings that never become second ones, and in a restlessness that won't let you sit through a whole conversation without reaching for your phone. At work, colleagues may have quietly started working around you. Mars rules your chart and hates waiting. Next time you walk in somewhere new, let the other person set the pace for the first few minutes, and match it.

sun.upright:
A Taurus Sun builds things to keep. You put down roots, make things solid, and like knowing that what you've gathered will still be there next year, and Death unsettles all of that. Scorpio sits straight across the zodiac from Taurus, the two ends of one axis, so this card is your opposite number come to argue the other side. Where you hold, it lets go. The elements are the saving grace. Earth and water are friends, each giving the other shape and something to grow in, so this opposition pulls toward balance as much as toward a fight.

What it feels like is a slow insistence that something you built to last has finished being useful and has started to cost you. You'll know the thing. Taurus digs in when pushed, so your first move is to hold on tighter, and the card doesn't argue back. It just waits, and it can wait as long as you can. Venus rules Taurus and likes what it likes, and a lot of Taurus Suns I've read for take real pride in being the one who never changes. There's nothing wrong with that. It does mean an ending feels like a personal failure here, even when it's ordinary upkeep.

Money and the body are where this usually lands. It's the possession or arrangement you keep out of habit, the subscription, the storage unit, the car nobody drives, that's become dead weight. It's also the comfort, the food, the long evenings on the couch, that used to restore you and now just sits heavy. Let go of one thing you've kept only because giving it up felt like a waste.
sun.reversed:
Taurus Suns with Death reversed can mistake gripping for strength. You keep the finished arrangement going because you paid for it, because it's always been done this way, because letting it fall feels like waste, and Scorpio's push to release runs straight into your heels dug in. The steadiness that's usually your best quality turns into inertia, and the axis tips all the way to your end.

It shows in money tied up in something that hasn't paid off in years, kept out of pride, and in a comfort you defend long after it stopped comforting you. Life gets heavy and slow, and your household stops suggesting changes because they already know the answer. Pick the most expensive thing you're keeping for no good reason and start the dull work of letting it go. Nobody says you have to enjoy it.

moon.upright:
For a Taurus Moon, safety is things staying where they are. The same bed, the same walk, the same people in the same chairs, the kettle on at the same hour. Death comes from the opposite side of the zodiac and asks you to let one of those fixed comforts go. That sounds brutal, and it's gentler than it sounds, because earth and water are friendly elements. The feeling and the change can feed each other here, and what grows afterwards tends to hold.

There's still a real ache in it. Something that soothes you has gone slightly off, and part of you knows. Venus rules Taurus, and a Venus Moon takes comfort through the senses, so you'll probably notice it there first, a favourite meal that doesn't hit the spot, a room that feels stuffy however often you air it, a person whose company you keep out of habit. Taurus Moons are loyal to their routines well past the point of pleasure. An opposition is an axis pulling for balance, and the other end of yours knows how to let go. You're being asked to borrow a little of that, and to be honest it'll feel strange for a while.

The body usually tells you before your head admits it, through bad sleep or a low, heavy tiredness after meals. At home it might be a piece of furniture, a habit, or an old arrangement with a housemate that's due to change. Change one small familiar thing on purpose and put up with feeling unsettled for a few days.
moon.reversed:
Comfort clamps down into a cage when Death turns over on a Taurus Moon. You eat the same things, see the same people, run the same evening, because change frightens the part of you that only feels safe when nothing moves. The grief that ought to pass through you gets no room, so it settles into the body, as heaviness, as a stomach that's never quite right.

It shows as comfort eating that's stopped comforting, a home that's gone stale, a small dread whenever someone suggests something new. A partner may have given up asking whether you'd like to try the place across town. Loosen one habit you hold onto for safety and let yourself feel wobbly for a day or two. Most of that wobble passes quicker than you expect.

rising.upright:
Taurus rising meets people slowly and solidly. Venus rules your chart, and strangers see someone calm and unhurried, pleasant company, a person who won't be rushed. Death arrives from the far side of the zodiac, Scorpio facing Taurus across one axis, and it's asking for the thing you're least keen on, which is movement. Earth and water get along, so the ask is a gentle one, the way a riverbank shifts over years.

You might feel that your steady, unbothered manner is keeping something at arm's length that actually needs dealing with. The calm reassures people, and it's also a very good way of never having to change. In the picture there's a bishop standing in front of the horse with his hands pressed together, as if he might be able to reason with it. That's a very Taurus-rising move, meeting an ending with composure and hoping it goes round you. It rarely goes round.

Strangers read you as unshakeable, which helps until they stop bringing you anything real because they assume you're fine. In new jobs and new groups you default to wait-and-see, and lately that may be costing you openings. On a first date it can come across as not being all that interested. The next time something new comes up, let your first answer be yes, before your usual pause, and see what it's like to move sooner.
rising.reversed:
Upside down on Taurus rising, Death leaves you wearing a face that never updates. You keep presenting the same unbothered calm while the ground underneath has shifted, and Scorpio's sense that something needs to end gets buried under your refusal to look ruffled. The calm stops reassuring anyone and becomes a way of not noticing.

Others take your steadiness to mean everything's fine, so they stop offering help you might need, and you end up the last to admit an approach has failed. At work it can read as a stubbornness people have learned to work around. With someone new it can look like mild boredom. Venus rules your chart and does best when it's warm. Let your face show it when something's hit you, and tell one person what it was.

sun.upright:
Gemini Suns need things moving. Mutable air, ruled by Mercury, you've usually got three conversations going and two projects on the boil, and you get restless the second things go still. Death is about as far from that as the deck goes. Scorpio stands five signs off from Gemini, the quincunx, with almost no common ground, and water and air are neutral to each other. They don't fight. They just have to be introduced on purpose, and nobody's made the introduction yet.

What you'll feel is the urge to change the subject the moment an ending gets heavy, to open a new tab, start a new plan, make a joke. To an air sign, Scorpio's depth can feel like being held underwater, and your reflex is to come up for breath and something lighter. The Lovers is Gemini's own card, and it's about choosing, which you do reluctantly because every choice shuts a door. Death shuts doors too, and it doesn't wait to be asked. The pairing wants you to let one thread end completely and feel the loss of it, without scattering into three new ones to cover it up.

At work it's the several projects you keep half alive so you never have to call one dead. In friendships it's the way you'll talk around a real goodbye for months, keeping it light in the group chat. Pick the one thread you keep reopening and close it properly, then hold off starting anything new for a few weeks.
sun.reversed:
Every ending gets explained away when Death is reversed for a Gemini Sun. You reframe it, find the clever angle where nothing really has to close, and Scorpio's demand for the whole truth disappears into a cloud of words. The restlessness that's normally part of your charm keeps you moving fast enough that no loss lands long enough to be felt.

You'll catch it in a dozen open loops, courses half done, chats left hanging, plans kept vaguely alive so none of them can end. Under the busyness there's usually a real fear of the quiet that comes after something's genuinely over. Mercury rules Gemini and likes having the last word. Next time you catch yourself explaining it again, stop halfway and let the pause sit. Then close one loop completely before you open another.

moon.upright:
A Gemini Moon works through a feeling by talking it out. You turn it into words, a long voice note, a chat at midnight, until it's small enough to handle. Death lands on that with a request you'll dread, to stop narrating a loss and just have it. Scorpio wants the feeling at full depth and mostly in silence. Gemini wants it explained, and ideally funny. The two signs are a quincunx apart, which is an itchy angle, and since water and air don't blend on their own, you'll have to build that bridge yourself.

The trouble is that talking, which usually brings relief, becomes the thing keeping the feeling at a distance. You can describe exactly how you feel, in fine detail, and still not have felt much of it, and some quiet part of you notices the gap and isn't fooled. Mercury rules Gemini, and it's quick enough that you can explain an emotion before it's finished arriving. I've watched Gemini Moons get so good at this that the people around them assume they're over something they haven't started grieving.

It shows around a friendship that's ended without anyone saying so, which you keep light with jokes. Sleep is the other place, where your head won't stop chattering long enough to let the sadness through. Try feeling one thing for a whole evening without putting it into words for anyone.
moon.reversed:
Noise becomes a way to outrun grief for a Gemini Moon with Death reversed. You fill every gap with input, a podcast, the group chat, a fresh topic, so the silence where the feeling lives never gets a chance to open. The mind stays busy precisely so the heart doesn't have to catch up.

This looks like a racing head at two in the morning, a cheerfulness that's working a bit too hard, and a habit of switching subject the instant a conversation gets near the real thing. The loss doesn't resolve. It just goes round and round. A sibling or an old friend is often the one who notices first. Put the phone in another room one evening and let the quiet stay quiet, even though your head will hate it.

rising.upright:
Gemini rising tends to be halfway into a conversation before anyone's been introduced. Mercury rules your chart, and people meeting you see someone quick, curious and hard to pin down, three questions in before the other person has sat down. Death on the mask asks for something that cuts right across that, a slower, heavier way into a room. Scorpio sits five signs from Gemini, the quincunx, so the card and your usual approach keep having to renegotiate, and air and water need a proper introduction before they'll work together.

You might notice the charm not quite catching. The easy patter that used to open every door is sliding off people, and your instinct is to try another angle, another topic, a better joke. What's actually wanted is a bit of weight. In the picture there's a child looking straight up at the rider and holding out a bunch of flowers, the plainest gesture anyone in that field makes. The plain approach may do more for you than any amount of cleverness would.

New people get the entertaining surface and don't come back for more. In fresh settings your quick read of the room keeps missing what's underneath. On a first date the wit can come across as nerves. Early in your next conversation with someone new, say one true, unclever thing, and notice who leans in.
rising.reversed:
With Death upside down, Gemini rising can turn cleverness into a smokescreen. You keep the talk fast and bright so nobody, yourself included, notices an approach that stopped working a while back. The quiet signal that something needs to end gets buried under the chatter, and you're moving too quickly for anyone to get a read on you.

People find you entertaining and somehow out of reach, so they stop bringing you anything heavy, and that leaves you lonelier than the busy surface suggests. You'll see it in first meetings that stay shallow by design and in a nervous need to fill every silence. At work it can mean being liked and never quite trusted with the serious stuff. Let a pause happen in your next conversation, and don't rush in to rescue it.

sun.upright:
Cancer Suns get their strength from caring, from making a safe place and keeping their people close inside it. Death moves through that easily, because both run on water. Scorpio and Cancer are four signs apart and share an element, a trine, the smoothest angle in astrology, so the card doesn't fight your nature. It deepens it. That's the gift and the danger together. Water on water turns the volume up, and endings you'd feel keenly anyway can pull you right under.

What it feels like is a quiet knowing that something in your care has reached its end. It might be a role you've played for a family, the one who does Christmas, the one everyone rings when something goes wrong. It might be a way of protecting someone who doesn't need protecting any more. Cancer holds on, so even while you sense it's finished you'll keep going, and the ease of the trine makes the holding feel like love. I've watched Cancer Suns keep a role like that going for years after everyone else had quietly moved on.

Home and family are where this lands. A child growing past the point of needing you to step in. A parent you can't keep safe however hard you try. Your moods will run deep for a while, and your household will notice. Let one person you've been looking after do a hard thing on their own, and stay out of it even when you're itching to help.
sun.reversed:
Protection can turn into a grip nobody can loosen when Death comes up reversed for a Cancer Sun. You keep mothering a bond that's meant to change, holding a person or a role in a shape that finished a while ago, and because Scorpio only adds more water here, the clinging runs deep and feels righteous. Care starts to look like control once it won't let anyone grow past you.

You'll find it in a family role you can't put down, in ringing a grown child every day, in running a parent's life for them. The tighter you hold, the more they pull away, which frightens you into holding tighter still. The Moon rules Cancer, and your mood sets the tone of the house whether you mean it to or not. Loosen your hold on one person you love and let them miss you for a while.

moon.upright:
The Moon rules Cancer, so a Cancer Moon is the Moon in its own sign, feeling at its most native, tidal, protective, tuned to home and to the past. Death speaks exactly the same language. Water meeting water four signs apart is all flow and no friction, which means grief moves through you completely once it starts. That's a real gift. You can feel an ending all the way down and come out the other side clean. It's also the risk, because the same openness can leave you swamped.

The card has landed on your need for safety, and it points at a comfort tied to the past that's asking to be let go. Cancer Moons hold onto everything. A voicemail you've never deleted, a jumper that still smells of someone, the street you grew up on and drive past on purpose. Letting go of even one of those can feel like betraying the memory. Most Cancer Moons I've read for find the memory is still there afterwards, clearer if anything, and the ache of holding it has eased.

It shows around the family home, around keepsakes and a few routines that are heavy with nostalgia. It shows in sleep and appetite as well, which follow your feelings closely and dip and lift with them. Grieve one old thing all the way through, and let yourself cry about it if that's what comes.
moon.reversed:
Flooded is the word for a Cancer Moon when Death turns over. You can't tell an ending you need from a loss you dread, and you go under in both. With nothing in the element to check it, one grief drags every old one up behind it, and you find yourself crying over things that finished years ago alongside the one in front of you.

Nights get lost to nostalgia, old photos at one in the morning, messages to people you haven't spoken to in years. There's clinging to places and people long after they've changed, and appetite and sleep that swing with every mood. Grieve the one thing that's actually ending and leave the older sorrows for another day. Ring someone who'll just sit with you.

rising.upright:
Cancer rising reads a room before saying a word. You pick up the mood, make people feel looked after before they know why, and your face shows every change in the weather. The Moon rules your chart. Death sits easily on all that because it's water on water, a trine, so the card doesn't clash with how you come across. It soaks into it. The upside is that you can meet an ending with real feeling and let it show. The risk is that strangers get whatever mood you're in, whether you meant to share it or not.

The card is pointing at the way you approach new people, and it suggests a protective habit in there has done its time. Cancer rising tends to lead with the shell. You check whether someone's safe before you open up, and that made sense once, maybe in a family or a school where it really wasn't safe. One old version of that guard has stopped protecting you and started keeping good people out. You might notice it most with people who've shown you nothing but kindness and still get the careful version.

With strangers, it shows as a warmth that's real and still somehow hard to get past. In new jobs or a new neighbourhood, it's hanging back and scanning for trouble that isn't there. Meet one new person without deciding in advance whether they're safe, and let them see you before you've finished checking them out.
rising.reversed:
When Death is reversed for Cancer rising, the shell goes up and stays up. You keep the protective front in place long after the threat has passed, reading every new face as a possible hurt, and Scorpio's depth turns ordinary caution into something close to a moat. People can see the friendliness and can't find a way past it.

They sense the guard and stop trying, and you take the distance as proof the world isn't safe. It becomes a loop, and it tends to show in first meetings where you give warmth and no real access, and in moods that colour how you greet everyone. Neighbours know your name and not much else. Let someone new in a little before you've decided they've earned it, and see what they do with it.

sun.upright:
Leo Suns want to be proud of something, and to be seen being proud of it. Fixed fire, ruled by the Sun, you build yourself by shining at the thing you're good at, and you like the room to notice. Death sits three signs from Leo, a square, and both signs are fixed, so neither of you is built to give way. It's the angle of friction that forces a move. The elements don't help either. Water on fire either puts it out or turns it to steam, and a card about endings landing on your Sun can feel like someone reaching for the light switch.

What's being pushed on is pride, usually pride in a role you were once admired for. The captain, the star of the office, the one who throws the parties, the one who holds the family together with a big laugh. Some version of that has had its day, and you probably felt it before anyone said a word. Fixed fire keeps going, though, so the likely first response is to perform it harder. Strength is Leo's own card, and if you look at it, nobody in it is raising their voice. I've seen Leo Suns come out of an ending like this warmer than they went in, once they stopped needing it to look good.

At work it may be a title or a reputation you keep polishing after the real job behind it has moved on. In love it can be the part you play for a partner, the generous, dazzling one, when what the relationship needs from you has changed. Choose one role you've outgrown and hand it over while people still think you're good at it.
sun.reversed:
Upside down on a Leo Sun, Death tends to get fought in public. You won't let the finished thing end, because ending it would mean being seen to lose it, so you keep the show going, louder, more generous, more charming. The fixed square between your sign and the card turns into a standoff you're mostly having with yourself. The Sun rules Leo and hates to dim.

It shows in a job title held onto for the status after the work itself has lost you, and in a relationship where you keep being the life of the party because being sad in front of your partner feels unbearable. The people close to you end up clapping for something that finished a while ago, and they get tired. Tell one person plainly that something you were proud of is over, and let them be kind about it.

moon.upright:
A Leo Moon settles when it feels special to someone. Being someone's favourite, being remembered, having a fuss made on your birthday, these aren't small things to you. They're how your body knows it's safe. Fixed fire, ruled by the Sun, you give warmth freely and you need some back. Death squares Leo from three signs off, two fixed signs locked at the angle that forces something to move, and water on fire is the element pairing most likely to hiss. What the card touches is a place where you used to shine for someone, and that place is changing.

It might be a friend who's got a new best friend, a child who doesn't need you the way they did, a parent who's gone quiet or gone. Grief asks you to be small and unwatched for a while, and a Leo Moon finds that very hard, because being unwatched feels like being forgotten. So the sadness can come out as pride. You go a bit grand, a bit cool, you stop ringing first. Fixed signs hold feelings a long time, and yours will stay loyal to the old arrangement well after everyone else has adjusted. To be honest, that loyalty is one of the loveliest things about you. It just needs somewhere to go.

With a partner, notice whether you're asking to be adored when what you actually need is comfort, which is a different request. In the body it can show as a flatness, a loss of sparkle, evenings where nothing appeals. Tell one person you feel a bit forgotten, in those words, and let them look after you.
moon.reversed:
With Death reversed, a Leo Moon can start staging the hurt. You won't say you're sad, so it comes out as a sulk that wants noticing, a big gesture that's really a test, a generous present bought to win back warmth you feel slipping. Pride blocks the plain admission, and the grief under it stays stuck, because a fixed Moon squared by a fixed card digs in from both sides.

It tends to show with a partner who's asked more than once what's wrong and been told nothing, and with friends, where you've gone quiet waiting to be chased. Sleep can suffer too, the mind replaying who said what at the party. The Sun rules Leo and needs warmth to feel alive. Ask for it directly from one person, without the performance, and accept whatever size of answer comes back.

rising.upright:
Leo rising comes into a room like it's been expected. With the Sun ruling your chart, what people notice first is warmth, the hair, the laugh, the way you make them feel they've been invited to something. Death meets that entrance at a square, both signs fixed, which means a real clash in how you arrive and not much room to wriggle. Look at the rider in the picture. Black armour, a plain skull, no flourish anywhere, and everyone in that field is reacting to it anyway.

You might find the big, bright first impression you've relied on isn't getting the reaction it used to. The joke lands a little flat, the charm feels like work, and you're more tired after parties than you'd admit. Leo rising tends to answer a cool room by turning the light up, and with water pouring onto your fire that mostly makes steam. Some older version of the way you present has come to its end, possibly one you built in your teens or twenties to be liked quickly. Being fixed, you'll hang onto it for a while. The people who used to be dazzled may want something steadier from you, and you've got it in you.

At work it may show as a reputation for being the fun one, which has stopped doing you favours in meetings where people want weight. On dates it's the performance that gets you a second drink and never a second date. Go into one new situation deliberately quieter than usual, listen for the first twenty minutes, and notice who comes to find you.
rising.reversed:
When Death is reversed on Leo rising, the shine goes up to cover a change you haven't faced. You're louder, better dressed, a bit too golden for the occasion, and people meet a big, bright front with nobody quite behind it. Fixed fire digs in on the way it's always been seen, and the square with Scorpio means the pressure to change keeps building behind the smile.

At parties you end up as the entertainment and leave feeling lonely. At work you might be keeping a public image going after the job underneath it has shifted, and first dates can turn into a show with an audience of one. The Sun rules your chart and it doesn't need a performance to be warm. Next time you meet someone, let them see you tired or unsure about one small thing, and keep talking anyway.

sun.upright:
Virgo Suns take pride in being useful. Mutable earth, ruled by Mercury, you build yourself through doing things properly, the job done well, the problem spotted early, the one person who actually read the whole document. Death comes at Virgo from two signs away, a sextile, which is a friendly angle, an open door. Earth and water help each other too, water giving earth something to grow in and earth giving water a shape. So this is one of the gentler ways for the card to land. The catch with a sextile is that the door doesn't walk through itself.

What Death asks of you is to stop fixing something, and that's harder than it sounds. There's a thing in your life, a system at work, a routine, a relationship you've been managing like a project, that isn't broken so much as finished, and you keep adjusting it because adjusting is what you know how to do. Mercury in Virgo is very good at finding the next small improvement, and it can keep you busy tweaking for years. The Hermit is Virgo's Major, a man who's gone off on his own with a lantern, and he'd probably tell you some things are best left alone once they're done.

At work it's the process you keep refining that the team quietly stopped using months ago. In health it might be a diet or a training plan you've rewritten a dozen times, when the real issue is that you've lost interest in it. Pick one thing you've been maintaining out of habit, stop servicing it, and see whether anyone notices.
sun.reversed:
A Virgo Sun under a reversed Death can turn an ending into a maintenance schedule. The thing is finished, you know it's finished, and you're still patching it on Sunday afternoons, because one more adjustment feels safer than admitting it can't be saved. Mercury rules Virgo and can always find something else to fix. The sextile's easy exit sits there unused.

It tends to show in a job you keep improving from the inside long after your heart left, and in a partner or friend you treat as a problem to solve. It shows in the body too, a tight stomach, lists written at midnight, a low hum of criticism mostly aimed at yourself. Write down what you'd stop doing if you were allowed to stop, and cross one item off by simply not doing it.

moon.upright:
Clean benches, bills paid, a day with a shape to it. That's what a Virgo Moon needs before it can relax, and when you're upset you'll usually tidy something. Mercury rules Virgo, so your feelings tend to turn into tasks, and a task you can finish is enormously comforting. Death arrives from a sextile, two signs off, and earth and water get on well, so the feeling this card brings can settle into your routines gently. It won't ambush you. It does want something, though, and it's the one thing a to-do list can't handle.

Grief doesn't tick off. You can sort the drawers, make the calls, write the list of everything that needs doing after an ending, and all of it helps a little and none of it touches the actual sadness. Virgo Moons tend to worry in place of feeling, because worry at least feels like work. You might catch yourself fretting about the gutters, the car's service, a small mistake at work, anything but the thing itself. The sextile is an easy opening, and you still have to choose to use it.

At home it shows as busyness around something that's changed, a housemate moving out, a pet gone, a routine that belonged to two people and now belongs to one. In the body it goes to the gut and to sleep. Leave one chore undone on purpose, sit down, and let yourself be sad about it for as long as it takes the kettle to boil twice.
moon.reversed:
The reversed card tends to bury a Virgo Moon's grief under chores. You clean, you plan, you find something wrong with yourself to correct, anything with a checklist, and the loss never gets a quiet minute. The friendly angle between Scorpio and Virgo goes unused while you prove to everyone, yourself included, how well you're coping.

It shows in a spotless kitchen during a week that felt hollow, and in a new self-improvement project started the day after something ended. The gut and the shoulders usually carry it. A partner may feel shut out by how capable you're being. Mercury rules Virgo and likes problems it can solve, and this isn't one of them. Sit with a friend who won't give you advice and tell them what you actually miss.

rising.upright:
Virgo rising arrives quietly and notices everything. Mercury rules your chart, and strangers tend to meet someone neat, observant and a little reserved, the person who's already spotted the typo and found a spare chair. Death approaches from a sextile, friendly and two signs apart, and water and earth work well together, so the card eases into how you come across slowly. There's no clash in it. It still asks for a change, and the change is in how you make yourself welcome.

Virgo rising tends to earn its place in a room by being useful. You offer to help, you fix the small thing, you make yourself needed before anyone has to decide whether they like you. It works, and it's also a bit of a hiding place. That habit, or one version of it, has done what it was for. You might notice people leaning on you and never quite getting to know you, or a new group treating you as the organiser when you'd hoped to be a friend. Letting it go feels exposed, because without the usefulness you're just a person standing there, and Virgo rising doesn't love being just a person standing there. Mutable earth adapts, though, and you'll get used to it faster than you think.

Starting a new job, it may be the helpful-junior reputation you've outgrown. At a party it's the kitchen, where you always end up washing glasses. Next time you arrive somewhere new, don't offer to help with anything for the first half hour, and see who talks to you.
rising.reversed:
Hidden behind competence is where a reversed Death leaves Virgo rising. You present as capable, organised and fine, correcting small things and managing the details, and whatever's ending inside you stays out of sight, including from you. The helpful front becomes a way of never needing anything from anyone, and people take you at your word.

After a first meeting, people remember you as pleasant and efficient and couldn't say what you're like. At work you're relied on constantly and asked about rarely. With someone new you might be so careful not to get it wrong that you never quite turn up. Mercury rules your chart and loves precision. Let one person see you flustered or unsure what to do next, and let them help.

sun.upright:
Libra Suns build themselves around getting things right between people. Cardinal air, ruled by Venus, you're the one who sees both sides, smooths the meeting, finds the version everybody can live with, and you're proud of being fair. Death is the sign next door. Scorpio follows Libra round the zodiac, and neighbouring signs have very little in common, each holding what the other hasn't got. Water and air are neutral to each other as well, neither friends nor enemies, and someone has to make the introduction. In this pairing that's you.

What Scorpio has that you don't is a willingness to let something end badly. You'd do almost anything to make a goodbye graceful, a friendship wound down with no hard feelings, a working partnership dissolved over a nice lunch. Sometimes that works. Sometimes the grace is what's keeping a dead thing going, because you can't find the fair way out and so you stay. Justice is Libra's own Major, and she holds a sword along with her scales. Libra Suns tend to forget the sword is there.

In a partnership, personal or business, it's the arrangement you keep balanced and polite after the real connection has gone. With friends it's the group you stay in because leaving would upset the balance. With a decision it's the one you keep deferring so nobody's disappointed. Say one true thing about an ending you've been smoothing over, and let it be a bit ugly.
sun.reversed:
Libra Suns can get stuck halfway through a goodbye when Death is reversed. You keep looking for the ending where nobody's hurt, and since it doesn't exist, nothing ends. The diplomacy that's usually your best quality turns into a way of never letting the hard sentence land, and Venus, which rules Libra, keeps everything looking lovely on top.

You'll find it in a relationship carried on out of politeness, in a business deal neither side will close, in a decision you've been thinking about for a year. The cost is a steady, tiring strain, the effort of holding a balance that isn't real. Pick the ending you've been postponing for the sake of harmony, tell the person involved, kindly, and accept that they may be upset with you for a while.

moon.upright:
A Libra Moon can't settle while someone in the room is upset. You feel it physically, the tension in a voice, the chair pushed back a bit hard, and you'll smooth it over before you've worked out how you feel yourself. Venus rules Libra, and your comfort comes through harmony, company, a pleasant evening with someone you like. Death comes from Scorpio, the sign next door, a neighbour you share almost nothing with, and water and air need a deliberate introduction. In practice that means you have to choose to feel this one.

When something ends, your first move is to look after everyone else's feelings about it. You check on the others, you make sure the goodbye is civil, you keep the mood up at the wake. By the time you get to your own sadness it's been managed so thoroughly you can barely find it. Libra Moons often borrow their balance from the people around them, and this card asks you to find some on your own, which Scorpio knows how to do and you mostly don't. It'll feel lonely at first. That's alright.

With a partner it shows as keeping things sweet while something between you has quietly changed. With friends it's being the one who organises the card and the flowers when someone leaves. Sleep may be restless, because unfelt things come back at night. Spend one evening alone, with no company and no messages, and let yourself feel exactly what you feel about the ending.
moon.reversed:
Libra Moons with Death reversed tend to buy peace with their own grief. You soothe everyone, agree to things you don't mean, keep the house pleasant, and the loss you're carrying never gets to be yours out loud. The harmony you're defending went hollow some time ago, and keeping it up takes most of your energy.

It shows in a relationship that's polite and tired, and in resentment you swallow to avoid a scene. The body holds it as a clenched jaw or shoulders that never quite drop. Friends get the lovely version of you and have no idea anything's wrong, and you may notice you only spend time with people who never ask hard questions. Venus rules Libra and loves ease. Let one person see you upset, don't fix the mood afterwards, and stay in the room while it's awkward.

rising.upright:
Look at the young woman in the picture, kneeling near the horse with her face turned away. She can't quite bring herself to look, and that's close to how Libra rising meets anything unpleasant. Venus rules your chart, and people meeting you see charm, good manners, someone easy to talk to who makes the first minute comfortable for everyone. Death comes from Scorpio, the sign right next to Libra, neighbours with little in common, and water and air don't blend unless someone makes the effort.

Something in your way of starting things has had its time, and it's usually the reflex to please. You agree in the first five minutes because disagreeing feels rude, you mirror people's opinions back to them, you soften anything with an edge. It's made you very likeable. It's also meant plenty of people have met a gracious surface and never found out what you think. Scorpio has the thing you're missing, an ease with being disliked, and it looks straight at whatever's in front of it. You're being asked to borrow a little of that, and in my experience it costs Libra rising a lot less than you'd expect.

In a job interview it's the answer you tailor to what you think they want. On a first date it's agreeing about the film you didn't like. At work it's the diplomat reputation that gets you invited to every meeting and never asked for a view. The next time you're introduced to someone, give an honest opinion on something small and hold it.
rising.reversed:
With the card upside down, Libra rising can turn pleasing into a full-time job. You accommodate everyone, agree with each person in turn, and whatever's changing in you never shows, partly because you're too busy reading the room to notice it yourself. Venus rules your chart and it wants to be liked, and here it's gone into overdrive.

People come away from meeting you charmed and unable to remember much you said. At work you're liked and nobody could say what you stand for. In dating you may be choosing people because they chose you. It's tiring, and you often feel it on the drive home. Disagree with one person politely about something that matters to you, and notice which of them respects you for it.

sun.upright:
This is your own card. Death is Scorpio's Major, so a Scorpio Sun drawing it is the sign meeting its own portrait, and there's something almost funny about that, as if the deck has just held up a mirror. Fixed water, ruled by Mars with Pluto as the modern co-ruler, you build yourself by going all the way in, to people, to work, to the truth under the polite version. Same sign, same element, so the card turns up everything you already are.

The risk isn't the one it would be for most signs. You're not likely to cling. You're more likely to cut too deep. When a Scorpio Sun decides something is over, it's often over in a scorched-earth way, the number deleted, the bridge burnt, the whole project binned when only one part of it had died. That feels honest. Sometimes it is. Sometimes it's the Mars side of your sign wanting a clean, fast finish because slow endings are unbearable to you. The card itself is patient, and it's asking you to end something at the right size, which is a skill even Scorpios have to learn.

At work it may be a role you've outgrown that you're tempted to quit dramatically, when a proper handover would serve you better. In a close relationship it's the all-or-nothing ultimatum you've been drafting in your head. Your drive to rebuild after a loss is strong, and it'll need somewhere to go. Take one thing that needs to end and end only the part that's actually dead.
sun.reversed:
Reversed, Death can turn a Scorpio Sun's gift for letting go against itself. You know exactly what needs to end and you hold it anyway, quietly, managing it from a distance, because for your sign giving something up can feel like giving up power, and that's the loss you fight hardest. Water poured into water with no way out goes still, and the intensity starts to sour.

It shows in a grudge kept going years after the other person has moved on, in an ex you still keep tabs on, and in a project you've stopped believing in and won't let anyone else take over. The people close to you feel the undercurrent without knowing what it is. Mars rules Scorpio and doesn't like surrender. Tell someone you trust about one thing you've been secretly holding onto, and let saying it be the start of putting it down.

moon.upright:
Scorpio Moons feel things at the bottom of the well. You trust slowly and completely, you remember everything, and you'd take a hard truth over a kind lie any day. Death is your sign's own card, so this is fixed water meeting its own portrait, and nothing slows the feeling on the way in. A grief here goes all the way to the floor. You're built to survive that better than almost anyone, and it's worth saying so.

The trouble with a same-element pairing is that it can't tell when enough is enough. A Scorpio Moon can make a home in a loss. You hold it close because it's yours, and letting it ease can feel like saying it didn't matter as much as it did. I've seen Scorpio Moons carry a grief for years out of loyalty to the person or the thing that was lost. Mars, your sign's traditional ruler, keeps some part of you on guard, and grief that's guarded tends not to move. What the card wants is for the tide to go out again once it's come in.

With a parent, a lover or a close friend, it's the ending you feel far more than you show, and may never talk about. In sleep it's dreams that do a lot of the processing for you, vivid and sometimes heavy. In the body it's the jaw and the gut. Let yourself grieve fully, then do one ordinary, living thing, a swim, a meal with a friend, to mark that you've come back up.
moon.reversed:
A Scorpio Moon with Death reversed can move into the wound and stay there. The loss is held so close and so privately that grieving becomes a way of keeping it, and the ending never quite finishes. Still water goes dark, and the feeling can turn into brooding, or a slow resentment that has more to do with fear than with the person you blame.

It shows as an old betrayal replayed at night, a person you won't forgive because forgiving would mean letting them go, and a body that holds it all in the jaw and the stomach. A partner may feel they're being punished for something someone else did. Mars rules Scorpio and keeps its guard up. Bring one buried hurt into the open with someone you trust, and let them see how much it still matters.

rising.upright:
Scorpio rising already comes into rooms a bit like this card comes across its field. Watchful, unhurried, giving little away and noticing a lot. Mars rules your chart, with Pluto as the modern co-ruler, and strangers often feel they've been read before they've said hello. Death is your Ascendant's own card, water meeting water, so there's no clash to speak of. It deepens what's already there, and the question is whether that's what you need.

What the card has its eye on is a layer of guard that's outlived its use. Scorpio rising builds its armour for good reasons, usually early, often in a house where it paid to be careful about what you showed. You still control the first impression tightly, deciding exactly how much anyone gets and when. The instinct under this card will be to close up further when things change, to go harder to read. That's the doubled water talking. What would actually help is letting one layer drop. People already sense the intensity. They don't need the mystery on top of it to take you seriously, and some of them would like to get closer and can't find a way in.

New colleagues respect you and can't work you out. On dates you ask all the questions and answer none. With neighbours or new friends it's a slight coolness you don't mean. Tell someone you've just met one true thing about yourself that you'd usually save for the third or fourth meeting.
rising.reversed:
On Scorpio rising, a reversed Death clamps the lid down. You meet everyone armoured, showing only what you've chosen, and a change happening inside you stays hidden even from people who could help. Pressure builds under a lid like that, and it leaks out as suspicion, a sharp edge in meetings, a habit of testing people before they're allowed anywhere near.

First meetings go the same way each time, with you reading everyone and revealing nothing, and the reputation for being formidable has started to feel lonely. At work people may be a little afraid of you, and you might like that more than is good for you. Mars rules your chart and it's quick to defend. Answer one personal question honestly the first time someone asks it, and notice that nothing bad happens.

sun.upright:
Sagittarius Suns build themselves by going further. Mutable fire, ruled by Jupiter, you're proud of being the one who'll try the new country, the new idea, the big question at dinner, and you like a life with the door open. Death is the sign just behind yours. Scorpio sits next to Sagittarius in the zodiac, neighbours with little in common, each with what the other lacks. Water and fire are opposed elements as well, and your optimism is the fire in this, the thing a card like Death can dampen.

What Scorpio has that you mostly don't is the patience to stay in the dark part. When something ends, your instinct is to turn it into a lesson straight away, find the meaning, book the trip, decide everything happens for a reason. It's a lovely instinct and it gets you through a lot. It also means some of your endings never quite finish, because you've set off for the next horizon before the last one closed. Temperance is Sagittarius's Major, a card about mixing things in the right measure, and a bit of Scorpio's stillness is what's missing from your mix.

In study or belief, it may be a way of seeing the world that stopped holding up a while ago and that you keep defending out of habit. In work or travel, it's the move you start planning the moment things get heavy. Stay put through one ending without making a lesson of it, and see what's there when you don't leave.
sun.reversed:
Reversed, Death has a Sagittarius Sun running. Every ending gets outrun before it can land, and you call it optimism, the next plan, the next place, the new philosophy that makes the old one unnecessary. The blunt honesty you're proud of goes strangely quiet about your own losses. Jupiter rules Sagittarius and always wants more, more plans, more places, more people.

It shows as a string of fresh starts, a trip booked the week something falls apart, a belief swapped for a new one so the old one never has to be mourned. Friends may notice you don't talk about what happened. Behind you there's often a trail of things half ended. Cancel one escape, stay in the uncomfortable middle of something, and let it be as dull and sad as it is.

moon.upright:
A Sagittarius Moon feels safe with an exit in view. Space, humour, a plan for the weekend, the sense that nothing's pinning you down. When things get heavy you'd usually go for a long drive before you'd sit and talk about it. Death comes from Scorpio, the sign next door, a neighbour that feels almost foreign to you, and water meeting your fire is an uncomfortable mix, one damping the other. This card asks your Moon to stay still inside a feeling, which is about the hardest thing it could ask.

Sagittarius Moons tend to move through grief by moving. You'll get busy, get philosophical, look on the bright side, and all of that is genuine, and some of it is a way of not sitting in the room with the thing. Jupiter rules Sagittarius, and a Jupiter Moon trusts that things work out, which they often do. The trouble is that sadness you skip doesn't go away. It follows you to the next place and turns up as restlessness, an itch to be somewhere else that you can't quite explain. Scorpio's way, which is to stay put and let it hurt, is the part your Moon is short of.

With friends it can look like keeping a goodbye cheerful so nobody has to cry. With family it's the phone call about hard news that you turn into a joke. In the body it's not being able to settle at night. Stay in one evening with no plans, and when the feeling turns up, don't reach for the bright side.
moon.reversed:
When Death turns over for a Sagittarius Moon, the urge to bolt gets strong. A feeling gets heavy and you're off, busy, social, planning, keeping the mood up so the grief never finds you sitting still. Freedom, which you love, becomes a way of leaving your own heart behind, and every ending turns into a plan before it's been felt.

It shows in a calendar packed so tight there's no room to be sad, and in a bright side you reach for so fast it sounds rehearsed. Sleep gets thin. A friend or partner may feel you've gone somewhere even while you're in the room with them. Jupiter rules Sagittarius and needs things to mean something. Look for the meaning in the loss itself, sitting still with it for an hour, before you go looking anywhere else.

rising.upright:
Sagittarius rising walks in friendly, funny and already half out the door to somewhere more interesting. Jupiter is your chart ruler, and people meeting you usually find someone open, blunt, easy to like and hard to hold onto. Death approaches from the neighbouring sign, Scorpio, which has almost nothing in common with you, and water on fire cools things down. The card is asking the breezy way you arrive to carry a bit more weight.

You might notice the cheerful, everything's-an-adventure entrance is taking real effort. Something in you has gone quieter and deeper, and keeping the show going is starting to feel like a performance. Sagittarius rising usually answers a flat reception by getting more upbeat, telling a bigger story, being more fun. It doesn't work so well this time. People respond better when they can see you care about something, which your style tends to hide. The blunt honesty you're known for helps here, so long as you point it at yourself as well. Temperance, your sign's Major, is about getting the measure right, and the measure here means staying in a conversation longer than you'd like.

In new settings it's the reputation for being the free spirit, which gets you invited to everything and trusted with very little. Colleagues enjoy the big first impression and don't take it seriously enough. Dating brings out the travel stories, which keep the other person entertained and at arm's length. In your next first meeting, tell one story about something that went wrong for you, and don't make it funny.
rising.reversed:
The reversed card can make Sagittarius rising cheerful to the point of being unreachable. You keep things light and keep the exits open, breezing past anything real, so no one sees what's changing underneath, and after a while you can't see it either. The free-spirit front turns into armour, and the more you insist you're fine and off somewhere, the harder you are to get hold of.

People are charmed on the first night and don't stay, so the circle gets wide and the close friends get fewer. There's a habit of changing the subject with a joke. At work you may be liked and not relied on. Jupiter rules your chart and makes everything bigger, including the act. Stay in one conversation after it gets uncomfortable, and let the other person see it's landed.

sun.upright:
Capricorn Suns build for the long haul. Cardinal earth, ruled by Saturn, you're proud of what you've climbed and what you've kept standing, and being relied on means a lot to you. Death reaches Capricorn from two signs off, a sextile, a cooperative angle, and earth and water feed each other, so this card can work with your grain. The opening is real. You have to use it, though, and using it means letting something go on purpose.

For Capricorn that's the hard bit. Letting go feels like losing, and losing feels like weakness, so your habit is to carry the finished thing a while longer. A role at work you've kept going out of duty. A family responsibility that belonged to an older version of the family. A plan made at twenty-five that you're still carrying out at forty because you said you would. Saturn is patient and dutiful, and it will grind on long past the point of use if nobody stops it. The Devil is Capricorn's own Major, and it's a card about chains people could take off if they noticed them. Some of your obligations are like that. The sextile makes this easier than you fear, and an ending can go into the plan like any other decision.

In your career it's the ambition that's quietly stopped mattering and still gets your evenings. At home it's a responsibility you shoulder for something that's already over, possibly a parent's expectation of you. Pick one heavy thing you're carrying out of duty alone, set a date to put it down, and keep the date.
sun.reversed:
Capricorn Suns with Death reversed can end up carrying a dead thing a very long way. You hold the position, the duty, the structure after the life has gone out of it, because stopping would feel like admitting you failed. Saturn rules Capricorn and respects endurance, and here endurance has become the problem. The sextile's easy exit sits unused while you set your jaw.

It shows in a career defended past all reason, a family role you can't lay down, and a standard you punish yourself for missing. The body pays for it, in the shoulders, back, knees and sleep. The people who love you watch you turn down help. Put one heavy thing down on purpose and see who picks it up, if anyone needs to.

moon.upright:
A Capricorn Moon feels safest when it's in charge of itself. Competent, self-sufficient, not needing anyone, feelings kept in a drawer you open when you've got time. Saturn rules Capricorn, and a Saturn Moon often learned early that someone had to be the grown-up. Death reaches you through a sextile, two signs apart, and water and earth get on, so the feeling this card brings can soak slowly into your defences without storming them. That's the good news. The harder news is that a sextile only helps if you reach for it, and reaching isn't your strong suit.

When something ends, you manage it. You organise the paperwork, make the calls, keep everyone else going, and you're very good at it. Somewhere in there your own loss gets filed under later, and later doesn't come. I've seen a lot of Capricorn Moons go through a big ending like a project manager and then come apart months afterwards over something small, a song in a shop, a jar in the cupboard with someone's handwriting on the label. The feeling was always going to arrive. This card suggests you let it arrive on purpose, while there's someone around to help.

At work it shows as throwing yourself into the job so you don't have to go home to the quiet. In the body it's tension in the jaw, the back, the knees, and sleep that doesn't restore you. With a parent it may be an old role you're finally allowed to set down. Tell one person you're not fine, and let them do something practical for you.
moon.reversed:
Self-sufficiency turns into a wall when a Capricorn Moon gets this card reversed. You cope, you handle it, you keep everything standing, and the grief never touches the part of you that would have to need someone. Saturn rules Capricorn, and here its control keeps you safe and alone at once. Feelings get filed as weakness and left in the drawer.

It shows in being the person everyone leans on and nobody reaches, and in achievements that sit on top of a loss nobody's mentioned. The back and the jaw carry it. Holidays get cancelled for work. A partner might describe you as wonderful in a crisis and impossible to comfort. Let one safe person past the wall, say what you've lost out loud, and notice the structure is still standing afterwards.

rising.upright:
Capricorn rising gets taken seriously at the first handshake. Saturn rules your chart, so people tend to read you as composed, capable and a bit reserved, the one who'd know what to do in an emergency. Death meets that from a sextile, friendly and two signs apart, and earth and water work well together, so the change comes in slowly, wearing down the edges of the front over time. It won't crack you open. It does want a layer gone.

The layer is usually the authority. Capricorn rising meets new people by being in control, and it's worked for you, probably since you were young and looked older than you were. That composure has done its job and is starting to cost you. People respect you and keep their distance. They assume you've got it handled, so they don't offer. They'd tell you more if you seemed like someone who ever got things wrong. Saturn likes rules, and you've probably got one about never being seen to wobble in front of strangers. That's the rule up for review, and the sextile makes it easier to drop than you'd expect.

At work it's the senior-looking front that keeps juniors from asking you anything. In a new friendship group it's arriving so polished that nobody quite relaxes around you. On a first date it can feel like an interview, with you running it. Next time you meet someone new, admit early that you don't know something, and let them explain it to you.
rising.reversed:
Capricorn rising can end up so composed under a reversed Death that nothing gets through. You present as permanently in control and unbothered, and the change going on in you stays sealed behind the authority. Saturn rules your chart, and when you're uneasy it makes you stiffer, more correct, more formal. Any sign that you might be grieving gets tidied away before anyone sees it.

The first impression is built on control and very little warmth, and being the one in charge all the time is lonely. At work people may admire you from a distance that never closes. In new friendships you might be waiting to be approached, which from outside looks like judgement. Let the composure slip with one person, tell them something's ended and it's been hard, and see that they don't think any less of you.

sun.upright:
Aquarius Suns live partly in their heads and partly in the future. Fixed air, ruled by Saturn and in modern astrology Uranus, you build yourself around ideas, principles, friends and causes, and you're proud of seeing the whole system clearly from a slight distance. Death squares Aquarius from three signs away, and both signs are fixed, so neither side bends easily and the friction keeps building until something moves. Water and air are neutral to each other, and this card is water right through, grief and depth and feeling, the register you tend to keep at arm's length.

Being fixed, you'll hold your position, and your position is usually that you're above the mess. You can explain exactly why something ended, the pattern, the cause, what you'd do differently, and still not have felt it. Aquarius Suns will describe a breakup like a case study while their voice gives them away. The Star is Aquarius's own Major, a woman pouring water into a pool and onto the land, and it's interesting that your sign's card, for an air sign, is so full of water. Some part of you knows how to feel things. Death wants that part involved.

With a group or a cause, it's the one you've outgrown and keep turning up for on principle. With friends it's someone you've drifted from and explained to yourself so thoroughly you never said you missed them. In love it's the distance you keep from your own heartbreak. Let one ending be personal, and tell someone how it felt without explaining why it happened.
sun.reversed:
An Aquarius Sun with Death reversed can float above an ending it won't feel. You analyse it, file it under a pattern you've seen before, and the cool distance that usually helps you turns into a way of making sure no loss ever quite reaches you. The fixed streak digs in, and you'd sooner be right about why it ended than sad that it did.

It shows in a friendship you've reasoned your way out of missing, in a cause you cling to long after your heart left it, and in a numbness you might mistake for being fine. Other people can find you hard to comfort because you won't admit there's anything to comfort. Saturn and Uranus both have a hand in your sign, and neither is very soft. Sit with one loss for an evening without analysing it, and let it be messy.

moon.upright:
An Aquarius Moon feels safest at a slight remove. You need space, independence, and the freedom not to be swamped by anyone's feelings, your own included. Friends are often how you settle, and a good conversation about ideas can calm you faster than a hug. Death squares Aquarius from three fixed signs away, and water and air don't meet unless someone introduces them. This card lives at the bottom of the feeling, exactly where your Moon prefers not to go, and a square doesn't let you avoid it for long.

When something big happens, you tend to go up. You watch your own grief from the ceiling, reach for perspective, talk about yourself in the third person without noticing. It's a real skill in a crisis, being the calm one who keeps a clear head. It's less useful when the crisis is yours, because the feeling doesn't go anywhere while you're up there. It waits, and it tends to leak out sideways, a strange flatness, a short temper with friends, a documentary that has you in tears for no reason you can name. Saturn is your sign's traditional ruler, and part of the detachment is Saturn protecting you from being overwhelmed. It's done its job, and you're allowed to come down.

With friends it's keeping closeness at a manageable distance while something between you ends. In sleep it's a busy head at night that lets the heart stay offline. Let one person pull you all the way into the feeling, and hold off on the big picture until you've been there a while.
moon.reversed:
Things go cold fast for an Aquarius Moon under a reversed Death. The moment a feeling turns intense you go cool and rational, watching your own loss from a safe height so it never lands. The independence that keeps you steady turns into isolation, and the grief waits underneath, patient and unfelt. Detachment starts to pass for peace.

It shows in being the friend who's always fine and treats a breakup like data, in keeping everyone at friend-distance so no ending can cost too much, and in a wired head in the small hours. A partner may feel they're talking to a very kind stranger. Saturn rules Aquarius and builds walls well. Let one person close enough to reach you, and stay there when it gets uncomfortable.

rising.upright:
Aquarius rising comes across as friendly and slightly apart. Saturn rules your chart in the old system and Uranus in the modern one, and new people tend to find someone interested, a bit unusual, easy to talk to and hard to pull all the way in. Death squares your Ascendant from three signs away, fixed against fixed, which means friction that forces a change in how you arrive. Water and air have to be introduced on purpose, and this card's depth keeps pressing on the distance you keep.

What's being asked is that you let some feeling show on the way in. Aquarius rising tends to meet people as the interesting observer, with a good question and a view on the system and very little about yourself. It's a style that works at conferences and parties and in any room where you're new. It may also be one you built to keep people at a set distance, and that part of it has done its time. You might notice people finding you fascinating and getting no closer, or a new group treating you as the clever one who doesn't need looking after. Being fixed, you'll resist changing the approach. The square keeps pushing anyway.

At a new workplace you're known for ideas and never asked how you're going. First dates stay on books and politics and never get near either of your lives. With neighbours it's a friendly wave and nothing else, for years. Next time you meet someone, tell them about something that happened to you that you actually minded.
rising.reversed:
Upside down, Death can turn Aquarius rising's cool into a force field. You keep everyone at the same careful distance, interesting and out of reach, and whatever's changing in you never shows. The independent front becomes a way of belonging to nobody, which you tell yourself is freedom. The fixed square keeps the pressure on, and you hold the pose anyway.

New acquaintances find you fascinating and never quite become friends. In groups you're known and not close to anyone, and there's a loneliness you'd sooner not look at too hard. At work you may be the one with ideas whom nobody thinks to invite to lunch. Uranus, your chart's modern ruler, likes to be different. Try being ordinary with one new person, and let them see something has affected you.

sun.upright:
Pisces Suns feel their way through life. Mutable water, ruled by Jupiter and in modern astrology Neptune, you're porous, kind, tuned to things other people miss, and you build yourself as much through what you sense as through what you do. Death flows straight into that. Scorpio and Pisces are four signs apart in the same element, a trine, the easiest angle in the zodiac, so this card doesn't fight your nature at all. Doubling the element doubles everything, the good and the too much.

The good is that you can let an ending happen. You'll feel it coming before anyone says it out loud, the change in someone's voice, the quiet in an office before a restructure, and you won't waste energy pretending it isn't happening. Pisces is better at letting go than most signs. The risk is the other side of the same thing. With so little friction, an ending can wash away your edges, and a loss in one part of your life seeps into all of it. Pisces also takes on other people's grief, and you can find yourself mourning something that was mostly theirs. The Moon is Pisces's own Major, a card of things half seen at night, which is a fair description of how a big ending can feel to you.

With the people you love, it's the ending you absorb so fully you're not sure whose it is. In your working life it's the job you've already left in your heart and not yet resigned from. Feel it all, then write down plainly what's ending for you and what isn't, so you know which part to grieve.
sun.reversed:
A Pisces Sun can lose itself in an ending when Death is reversed. Water pours into water with nothing to hold it, so a loss swamps you, and you drift, soften the edges, blur it until you're not sure what's yours to grieve. The compassion that's normally your gift starts to feel like having no skin.

It shows in escape, too much sleep, too many screens, the extra glass, a fog that keeps the ending at a soft distance. It shows in a habit of taking on everyone else's sadness so there's never time for yours. Jupiter and Neptune, your sign's rulers, both like to expand and dissolve things. Come back to one solid thing, a walk, a meal, a friend's kitchen table, and name the one loss that's actually yours.

moon.upright:
A Pisces Moon needs softness. Somewhere quiet to drift, music, water, sleep, time to feel part of something bigger and to slip away when the world gets sharp. Jupiter rules Pisces, with Neptune as the modern ruler, and your feelings have very few walls. Death speaks exactly that language. Same element, four signs apart, a trine, so grief moves through you with no friction at all and gets all the way in before you've braced.

That's a real gift. You can feel a loss completely, cry properly, and come out the other side without the scar tissue other Moons build up. The difficulty is knowing where it stops. Pisces Moons pick up feeling from everywhere, the news, a friend's divorce, a stranger on the train, and when you're grieving something of your own the door is wide open to all of it. You can end up in a sadness the size of the sea without being able to say what it's about. What helps is having one solid thing to come back to.

With family or a partner it's the ending you feel in your whole body before a word's been said. In sleep it's long, vivid dreams that do a lot of the grieving for you, and mornings when you wake up tired. Let it move through you, then pick one steady thing, a person, a routine, a walk to the same bench, and go back to it every day while this passes.
moon.reversed:
Swamped is how a Pisces Moon tends to feel when Death is reversed. You let a loss wash out every edge you have, take on grief that was never yours, and drift until you can't find the bottom or the shore. The ending never finishes, partly because there isn't enough of a separate you to finish it.

It shows as retreat, into sleep, fantasy, a screen, something to take the edge off, and into the sorrows of people you look after so you needn't face your own. The body feels heavy and checked out. Friends may say you seem far away. Neptune, your sign's modern ruler, loves a fog. Find one anchor, a person, a room, your feet on a real floor, and grieve the single loss that's yours before it spreads into everything.

rising.upright:
Pisces rising meets the world softly. Jupiter rules your chart, with Neptune as its modern co-ruler, and strangers tend to feel understood by you before they know why, because you mirror them, gently, almost without meaning to. Death sits very easily on that. Water to water, four signs apart, a trine, so the card doesn't jar. It seeps into how you come across and gives it more depth. People may find you quieter and more serious, and readier to talk about something real.

It's the mirroring that's up for change. Pisces rising can become whatever each new person needs, and that's a lovely gift in a nurse, a teacher, a friend at a hard time. It can also mean nobody actually meets you. The softness was probably learned early, as a way of keeping things calm around you, and some of it has outlived the reason. With doubled water there's no friction to stop you blurring, so keeping an outline takes a conscious choice. You might come home from a party tired and a bit empty, having been six different people in one evening. The trine means the change can happen easily once you decide to let it.

In a new job it's the colleague everyone confides in and nobody can describe. Dating can mean agreeing so smoothly that the other person leaves thinking they've met their twin. With new friends it's taking on their mood as soon as they walk in. Next time you meet someone, mention one thing you like that they probably don't, and leave it there.
rising.reversed:
Pisces rising can dissolve into whoever's in front of it when Death is reversed. You shape-shift to fit each room so completely that whatever's changing in you disappears, and even you lose track of your own outline. The soft, adaptable front becomes a way of never being a fixed thing anyone could hold onto, or let down.

The first impression feels intimate and gives nothing away, and underneath there's a tiredness that comes from being made of other people. At work you may agree to things you'd never have chosen. In dating it can mean becoming a different person for each partner. Neptune is your chart's modern ruler, and it makes blending in very easy. Hold one small opinion of your own with someone new, and keep it even when agreeing would be easier.

1.upright:
Your body, your bearing, the way you start things and the face you lead with all sit in the first house. It's angular, one of the four corners of the chart, so what happens here tends to show quickly. With Death drawn into it, an old way of presenting yourself is coming to an end, and the change is likely to be visible. People may notice before you've said anything, a different haircut, a different way of standing, a quieter way of walking into a room.

This house belongs naturally to Aries and to Mars, and Scorpio sits five signs from Aries, the awkward quincunx, where two signs share almost nothing and have to keep adjusting. Water on this house's fire makes steam. There's one real thread between them, since Mars traditionally rules Scorpio as well as the first house, so the drive is the same even if the direction isn't. What that feels like is wanting a fresh start and not being able to make it take, because something about the old you hasn't finished yet. Mercury has its joy in this house, and a lot of the change happens in how you talk about yourself. You might catch yourself using a description that's stopped being true.
