In the body it can show as a routine or a way of dressing that no longer suits the person wearing it. With new people it's the introduction you've given for years and are a bit tired of giving. With anything you're starting, it's a reluctance to launch until the last version is properly done. Drop one description of yourself that's out of date, and notice what you say instead.
1.reversed:
In the first house, a reversed Death usually means you're still presenting a self that's finished. You reintroduce the old you, louder, because starting fresh would mean admitting a version of you is gone, and this is an angular house that hates standing still. The Mars energy that rules this corner of the chart gets spent defending an identity that's already past its use.

It shows as restlessness with nowhere to go, a body braced for a beginning it won't allow, a reinvention announced and never made. Friends may hear the same plans for the new you several times over. It can show in how you dress too, in clothes from a life you've already left. Pick one habit that belongs to the old version of you, and drop it for good.

2.upright:
Your income, your savings, the things you own, and what you believe you're worth. That's the second house. It's succedent, the kind of house that builds up and holds, and its natural sign is Taurus, ruled by Venus. Scorpio sits straight across from Taurus, the opposite end of the same axis. Taurus keeps and Scorpio lets go, so Death here is the far end of this house pulling it toward balance. Water and earth are friendly, which softens it. The ending can sink into this ground and clear it without too much of a wrench.

What's live is an arrangement around money or self-worth that's finished. It might be an income stream that's dwindled, a way of earning you've outgrown, or an old yardstick for your value that doesn't measure anything true any more. The house wants to hold on, and letting go of anything here can feel like losing security itself. That fear is worth looking at, because often the thing you're gripping costs you more to keep than it gives back. Scorpio also has a lot to do with shared resources, so the change may come through someone else's money, a joint account, a loan, an inheritance.

With income it can be a job or a client you keep for the money long after it stopped being worth it. With possessions it's the furniture from a previous home, the gear from a hobby you've dropped, things you keep because giving them away feels wasteful. With self-worth it's a price you charge that belongs to an earlier version of you. Sell or give away one thing you've kept only out of habit, and raise one price that's out of date.
2.reversed:
A reversed Death in the second house tends to show as gripping. You hold onto a resource, an income or a self-image long after the life went out of it, because selling, closing or admitting the number's changed feels like a small death. The house's Taurus side digs in at the wrong end of the axis, guarding a form of security that's already empty.

It shows as money tied up in something that hasn't paid for years, as prices you won't raise, and as a low, physical anxiety about scarcity that no amount of saving eases. Sometimes it's the opposite, spending so you don't have to feel a loss. Look at the one financial thing you've been refusing to look at, the account, the debt, the valuation, and read the actual figure.

3.upright:
Messages, siblings, neighbours, the short drive, the course you're doing, the way you think things through. The third house holds all the small daily traffic of a life. It's a cadent house, where things get processed and learned. Its natural sign is Gemini, ruled by Mercury, quick and light and curious, and Scorpio sits five signs off, the quincunx, with very little in common. Water and air are neutral, so they have to be walked toward each other deliberately. The Moon has its joy in this house, which gives it more feeling than people expect.

With Death here, something in how you talk and think is ending, usually a story. A version of events you've told for years about your family, a job, why a friendship went wrong. It's worn thin and you can feel it, even while you keep telling it. The house would prefer to keep things moving and keep them brief, and the card wants you to stop and say the harder, plainer thing underneath. That friction is uncomfortable. You might find conversations circling a topic without landing, or a group chat you used to love starting to feel like noise.

With a brother or sister it can be a way of relating that you both outgrew years ago and still act out at family lunches. In your street or suburb it may be a routine or a local connection that's quietly finished. In learning, it's a subject you've stopped caring about. Retire one story you tell about yourself, and next time the subject comes up, say what actually happened.
3.reversed:
When Death lands reversed in the third house, the ending gets talked about and never finished. You explain, reframe, ask everyone's opinion, keep the conversation running so the real goodbye never has to be said. Mercury's quickness keeps you out of the quiet where something could actually close.

It shows in a group chat going over a decision your gut settled weeks ago, in a matter with a sibling that gets raised every visit and never resolved, and in a jittery, overthinking head at night. Siblings or neighbours may be tired of hearing about it and too polite to say so. Writing it down once, properly, and then putting the page away can help. Stop the next conversation about it halfway, say you've said enough, and leave it closed.

4.upright:
Home, family, and the private ground nobody outside ever sees. The fourth house is one of the chart's four corners, angular and active, so a change here tends to set the tone for everything else. Its natural sign is Cancer, ruled by the Moon, and Scorpio sits four signs away in the same element, a trine. Death flows straight into this house without resistance, and water on water amplifies, so whatever ends here is felt all the way down.

What's ending is usually a form of home, or a role within the family. The house you grew up in being sold. The big family meal you've always hosted. Being the child who rings every Sunday, or the parent who's needed every day. It might be the shape of the household itself, someone moving out, someone moving in. Because the trine makes it so easy for feeling to move, you may find yourself grieving far more than seems proportionate, old family stuff coming up alongside the new. That's normal for this pairing. The ease is also the risk, because the place you usually go to feel safe is the place that's changing.

In the actual house it might be a room that's become a shrine to someone who's grown up or gone, or a renovation you've been putting off because it would change how the place feels. With parents it can be a shift in who looks after whom. With the people you live with, it's an old arrangement everyone's quietly outgrown. Choose one thing at home to change, clear out or give away, and do it with someone who'll understand what it means.
4.reversed:
The fourth house with Death reversed often holds a grief that won't drain. You keep the family arrangement, the old role or the old form of home going, because letting it end feels like losing the people themselves, and the easy trine makes the clinging feel like love. Water pools in the foundations, and the whole house sits a bit heavier for it.

It shows in a household still running on an arrangement everyone privately knows is over, a bedroom nobody's allowed to change, a family ritual everyone dreads and nobody will cancel. You may carry the weight home every evening without naming it. Let one old thing in the family reach its end, a tradition, a role, a conversation you've been having for twenty years, and see who's relieved.

5.upright:
The fifth house is the part of life that exists for pleasure. Romance, creativity, children, hobbies, parties, whatever you do on a free afternoon because it lights you up. It's succedent, a house that builds and keeps, and Venus has her joy here. Its natural sign is Leo, ruled by the Sun, and Scorpio squares Leo, both fixed signs, so this is friction that keeps building until something moves. Water on the house's fire is the least comfortable mix in the chart, and there's some hard rubbing between this card and this house.

What's finishing is a form of delight. A creative style you've outgrown, a band or a sport or a hobby that's stopped being fun and turned into an obligation, a romance that sparkled once and has gone flat. Leo's side of the house wants to keep performing the old joy, because admitting it's over feels like losing your spark. Being fixed, both signs dig in, and you may keep turning up to something long after the pleasure's gone, out of pride or habit or loyalty to who you were when you loved it. Venus having her joy here helps, since she knows what actually gives you pleasure and can tell when it's stopped.

With children, yours or someone else's, it can be a stage of childhood ending, and games you used to play together no longer being wanted. In romance it's a relationship that was all fun and now needs more weight, or needs to end. In creative work it's a style or a medium you keep going back to that no longer says anything. Let one pastime go properly, and use the free evening to try something you'd be bad at.
5.reversed:
Reversed in the fifth house, Death usually means a pleasure being kept alive on willpower. You keep the hobby, the flirtation, the creative routine going, brighter and more insistent, because this fixed house won't admit the fun has gone out of it. The Sun rules the fifth by nature, and its pride hates being seen to let a delight go.

It shows in art reworked long past the point it's alive, a romance kept up mainly for the look of it, and a social life that's become a performance. With children it can be holding onto a stage they've already left. Underneath there's a flatness nobody sees. Stop forcing one old pleasure and leave the time empty for a while, until something you actually want turns up.

6.upright:
Most of a life happens in the sixth house. The work you do each day, the commute, the lunches, the chores, and the upkeep of the body, sleep and food and exercise. It's cadent, a house of adjusting and processing. Virgo is the natural sign here, with Mercury as ruler, and Scorpio sits two signs away, a sextile, which is an open door that still has to be walked through. Water and earth suit each other. Mars has its joy in the sixth, and Mars is Scorpio's traditional ruler, so this card has a foothold here. It knows how to work.

What's ending is a routine. A way of working, a daily habit, a regime for the body that did its job and has turned into a rut. Virgo's side of the house would much sooner fix a routine than end it, so the likely first move is to tweak it, add a new app, change the time of day, and wonder why nothing's shifting. Often the body has noticed before you have, through a tiredness that no amount of adjusting touches. Take that as a sign an old pattern has had its day. It isn't a verdict on anything.

At work it can be a task or a role you've done so long you could do it asleep, which is partly the problem. In health it's an exercise habit or a way of eating that suited a different stage of life. With pets or anyone you look after daily, it may be a care routine that's changing because their needs have changed. Stop one daily habit for a few weeks and see what fills the gap.
6.reversed:
In the sixth house, a reversed Death turns into endless maintenance. You keep servicing a dead routine, adjusting a way of working that's already over, sure that one more tweak will fix what's actually finished. The sextile's open door stays shut while you tidy and optimise, and the effort wears you down.

It shows in a job kept patched together, a fitness plan rewritten for the fifth time, a daily grind you defend because stopping would feel like slacking. Colleagues may have stopped noticing how much you do, because you've done it the same way for years. The tiredness is real, and it's asking for gentler upkeep, a proper lunch break, an earlier night, fewer rules. Let one finished routine stay finished, and put the time into rest you'd actually enjoy.

7.upright:
Across from you in the seventh house sits a partner, a business partner, anyone you've made a real one-to-one agreement with, and sometimes an open rival. It's angular, one of the chart's corners, so changes here tend to be visible and hard to ignore. Libra is its natural sign, ruled by Venus, and Scorpio is the very next sign along, a neighbour with little in common. Water and air have to be introduced deliberately. So Death in this house brings depth into a place that usually runs on fairness and good manners, and the two don't automatically understand each other.

What's live is an ending inside a partnership. Sometimes that's the partnership itself. More often it's a form of it, a way of being together that's finished, an agreement that needs redrawing, a role one of you has played for years and can't keep playing. Libra's side of the house wants the change handled gracefully, with nobody hurt. Scorpio's side wants it honest. Those two pull differently, and you may find yourself keeping things pleasant and polite while something at the root has already shifted. Each sign has what the other lacks, so there's something to learn from the awkwardness.

With a partner, it might be the conversation about what's changed between you that neither of you has started. In business it's a contract or a collaboration that needs ending or rewriting. With a close friend it can be a dynamic where one of you always leads. Say the true thing about what's changed to the person across from you, and let the conversation go wherever it goes.
7.reversed:
A reversed Death in the seventh house tends to leave a partnership hanging. You weigh it endlessly, look for the fair goodbye where nobody's hurt, and since that doesn't exist, the bond stays half alive. Venus keeps the surface pleasant while the connection underneath has already gone somewhere else. The balance you're protecting has stopped being a real one.

You'll see it in a partnership that carries on out of habit, a contract neither side will sign off, a business partner you avoid and still depend on. There's a low, constant strain in it, a smile held over something finished. Friends can see it from outside and have stopped asking. Decide whether the bond needs ending or rebuilding, then say so to the other person, even if the conversation is clumsy.

8.upright:
This is the card's own house. The eighth covers shared money, debt, inheritance, intimacy and sex, and the endings that change a life, and its natural sign is Scorpio, the sign Death belongs to. Mars rules it traditionally and Pluto in modern astrology, the same rulers as the card. It's a succedent house, where things accumulate, and with the same element on both sides, water on water, Death here is about as concentrated as it gets.

That means an ending in this territory is likely to be thorough. The eighth doesn't do half measures, and neither does this card. It may be a change in how you share, a joint account being split or merged, a debt finally paid off or finally admitted, an estate being settled. It may be a change in intimacy, a closeness deepening because something false between you has ended, or a sexual relationship that's finished. There's very little to soften it, which is the risk, and things can feel total. What helps is remembering that this house has always been where you end things and start again, and you've done that before.

With a partner's money or joint property, it's the time to look at the real arrangement and change what's finished. With intimacy it's honesty about what you want, which may be different from what you wanted a few years back. With family money it can be a will, an inheritance, or a long-running debt that needs closing. Sit down with the person you share resources with, bring every document, and end one arrangement that no longer suits either of you.
8.reversed:
In the eighth house, a reversed Death is usually an ending gripped in secret. You keep control of the shared money, the intimacy or the arrangement from behind the scenes, because in this house letting go can feel like losing power, and that's the loss you resist hardest. Water with no outlet turns dark and still, and a lot of what's stuck here is never said out loud.

It shows in a joint arrangement kept going past its end, in closeness offered out of fear of the alternative, in a debt or a secret about money that someone else doesn't know about. It can come out sideways as jealousy or control. Bring one hidden ending into the open with the person it concerns, plainly, and let them respond.

9.upright:
The ninth house is where you go looking for meaning. Belief, study, long trips, other cultures, the big questions about what your life is for. It's cadent, a house of learning and letting go, and the Sun has its joy here. Its natural sign is Sagittarius, ruled by Jupiter, and Scorpio sits right next to it, a neighbour with little in common. Water on the house's fire makes steam, and the house's optimism doesn't always like what this card brings. It's worth looking past the rider in the picture to the far background, where the sun is coming up between two towers.

What's finishing is a way of seeing the world. It might be a faith you grew up in and have quietly stopped believing, or a political view that no longer fits what you've seen, or a course of study that made sense when you started and doesn't any more. Sagittarius's side of the house wants to replace it straight away with something shinier, a new teacher, a plan to move overseas, a new theory. Scorpio's side wants you to sit with the fact that something you believed has died. That's uncomfortable, and I'd guess part of you has known for a while.

With study, it could be a qualification you're halfway through and don't want. With travel it's a place you always go back to that's stopped feeling like yours. With in-laws or people from a different background, it may be an old assumption about them that's worn out. Before you pick up a new belief or plan, write down what you used to believe and what changed your mind.
9.reversed:
A dying belief tends to get replaced before it's grieved when Death is reversed in the ninth house. You swap the worldview, book the far trip, sign up for the next course, so you never have to sit with a faith or a plan that's ended. Jupiter's appetite for more keeps you starting over, and the old meaning trails behind, unmourned.

It shows in a philosophy defended well past the point you believe it, in a study started to avoid finishing the last one, and in a belief system changed like a coat. There's a restlessness that no new horizon quite fills. Stay with one lost belief for a while, talk to someone about what it meant to you, and hold off on replacing it.

10.upright:
Career, reputation, your public role, what strangers would say you do. The tenth house is the most visible corner of the chart, right at the top, and it's angular, so what happens here gets seen. Capricorn is its natural sign, ruled by Saturn, and Scorpio sits two signs away, a sextile, a cooperative angle that still has to be used. Water and earth get on well together, so the card can work with this house's structure instead of knocking it over.

What's ending is a public role or identity. A job title, a position in an organisation, a professional reputation for being a certain kind of person, the founder, the fixer, the reliable number two. The house is built for long, patient ambition, and it tends to treat stepping down as failure. So the instinct is to keep climbing, keep polishing, keep the role going on willpower after the real thing behind it has changed. The sextile says an easier ending is available, a handover, a planned exit, a change of direction that people will respect. You do have to reach for it.

At work, it might be a role you've outgrown and are too loyal to leave, or a promotion that's really an invitation to stop doing what you're known for. With your reputation, it's being known for something you did years ago and are tired of being asked about. If you run your own business, it might be a product or a service line that's had its day. Write down the role you'd step out of if nobody would think less of you, and have one conversation about how to do it well.
10.reversed:
The tenth house with Death reversed keeps a public role standing after the life has gone out of it. You defend the title, keep climbing, hold the reputation together with sheer effort, because Saturn here reads stepping down as defeat. The sextile's clean exit goes unused while you grind on at a height that's stopped meaning much.

It shows in a career kept going for the look of it, in status guarded well past sense, and in a role that's become a costume you put on in the car park. It costs you sleep, and it costs the people at home their evenings with you. Colleagues may see it before you do. Tell one person you trust what you'd do if you stopped, and listen to how it sounds out loud.

11.upright:
Friends, groups, teams, the people you'd message with good news, and the hopes you carry for how life might turn out. That's the eleventh house. It's succedent, a house that builds up over time, and Jupiter has its joy here. The natural sign here is Aquarius, ruled by Saturn and in modern astrology Uranus, and Scorpio squares Aquarius, fixed against fixed, which is friction that forces a move. Water and air don't mix unless someone makes them.

What's ending is a circle or a hope. A friendship that's quietly finished, a group you've outgrown, a community you joined for a reason that no longer applies. Sometimes it's a picture of the future, the life you were aiming at in your twenties, which doesn't fit who you've become. Aquarius's side of the house holds on out of principle. You said you'd be there, so you keep turning up. Scorpio's side knows when something's over. The square won't let this sit still for long, and you might find yourself getting irritated with people you used to love, which is often how an ending first shows itself here.

With friends it's the group chat you mute and don't leave, or the friend you see out of duty. In a club, a team or a cause, it's the role you took on years ago and would hand over in a second if anyone asked. With your hopes it's a long-held plan you keep for loyalty's sake. Leave one group or step back from one role, kindly, and spend the time with the friends you'd call first in trouble.
11.reversed:
In the eleventh house, the reversed card usually means staying in a group your heart left a while ago. A fixed house won't admit a friendship or a future is done, so you defend the old dream and keep showing up, and the belonging goes hollow while you insist it's fine.

It shows as a friendship group you've outgrown and won't leave, a cause kept up past your belief in it, and a future you cling to because it belonged to who you used to be. There's a quiet loneliness in the middle of the crowd. Jupiter's joy in this house needs real warmth to work with. Let one finished tie go, and give the time to the two or three people who'd still turn up if you needed them.

12.upright:
Sleep, dreams, retreat, and the things you don't quite admit to yourself belong to the twelfth house, along with the places people go to recover, a hospital, a quiet room, a week away from everyone. It's cadent, where things are processed and let go. Its natural sign is Pisces, ruled by Jupiter and in modern astrology Neptune, and Scorpio sits four signs away in the same element, a trine. Death moves through this house with almost no friction.

That's both the ease and the danger. Endings here tend to be private ones, the kind nobody else knows you're going through. You may feel something has changed inside you without being able to say what, a tiredness with no clear cause, dreams that keep going back to the same house or the same person, a pull toward being alone. Saturn has its joy in this house, which is interesting with this card, because a bit of structure helps here. A regular bedtime, a set time for quiet, a practice you keep up. It gives what's ending somewhere to surface.

In sleep, pay attention to what your dreams keep bringing up, since that's often the first place this shows. In private habits it might be a comfort you rely on that's stopped comforting. With anyone you care for quietly, visiting, nursing, keeping company, it can be the end of that role. Keep a notebook by the bed, write down what you dream and what you're sad about for a few weeks, and read it back.
12.reversed:
Buried grief is the usual story when Death sits reversed in the twelfth house. A loss you haven't named steers you from somewhere out of sight, and because the water runs so deep here, you can stall for a long time without knowing why. The retreat that ought to restore you becomes a place to hide.

It shows as tiredness you can't trace, sleep that doesn't help, an escape into screens or solitude that doesn't heal anything, and a vague sense of being stuck. It can come out in odd ways, a flash of anger over nothing, a day in bed you can't explain. People around you may have no idea anything's wrong. Say the buried loss out loud to someone you trust, in daylight, and then book some real rest with nobody to look after.
